scenario: One mountinfo line carries four optional fields (shared:1 master:2 propagate_from:3 unbindable) before the separator and describes an xfs mount at /srv/data whose super options are rw,noquota,attr2,inode64; the two reported paths (/srv/data, and the nested /srv/data/reports) both resolve to that mount, and a further tmpfs line follows it so the xfs super options are not the last field of the mountinfo text.

fixture.mountinfo:
21 25 0:19 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime - proc proc rw
22 25 0:20 / /sys rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime - sysfs sysfs rw
23 25 0:21 / /dev rw,nosuid,relatime - tmpfs devtmpfs rw,size=4096k,mode=755
27 1 0:24 / / rw,relatime - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache=v1,subvolid=5,subvol=/
29 21 0:26 / /srv rw,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=16384k
31 29 0:25 / /srv/data rw,relatime shared:1 master:2 propagate_from:3 unbindable - xfs /dev/mapper/data rw,noquota,attr2,inode64
32 21 0:27 / /run rw,nosuid,nodev,relatime,size=1638404k - tmpfs tmpfs rw,mode=755

rationale: Corrected under the round-23 pre-seal amendment (preseal-amendment.md, C2 final rules). DELTA FROM THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL: the single btrfs_sysfs record (a decoy uuid that no reported path resolves to) gains the required member 'qgroups_enabled' with value null, because its 'qgroups' is false and the amendment requires qgroups false to pair with enabled=null/mode=null; record keys are now exactly devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode. Mountinfo text, paths, device_links, expected values, id and scenario are preserved unchanged from the original proposal, because the amended rules confirm rather than change the derivation. DERIVATION: (1) Parsing - the amendment requires the separator and the last THREE fields of EACH chosen line, never file-wide; the '/srv/data' line is '31 29 0:25 / /srv/data rw,relatime shared:1 master:2 propagate_from:3 unbindable - xfs /dev/mapper/data rw,noquota,attr2,inode64', i.e. fixed fields 1-6 (mount ID 31, parent ID 29, major:minor 0:25, root '/', mount point '/srv/data', mount options 'rw,relatime'), the optional tag[:value] block 'shared:1 master:2 propagate_from:3 unbindable' (all four are valid optional fields per S082 proc.rst 1988-1993, and the layout is fixed by S082 proc.rst 1973-1983), the separator '-', then fstype 'xfs', mount source '/dev/mapper/data' and super options 'rw,noquota,attr2,inode64' as the last three fields of that line. The trailing '/run' tmpfs line is a different line and its super options 'rw,mode=755' are not in scope. The mountinfo text contains no backslash escape, so the amendment's octal-decoding rule (040/011/012/134, other escapes rejected as QUOTA_SETUP) is not engaged, and the text's single trailing newline yields one empty trailing line, which the amendment says to ignore. (2) Election - the amendment keeps longest component-prefix selection; covering mount points for '/srv/data' are '/', '/srv' and '/srv/data', and for '/srv/data/reports' likewise '/', '/srv' and '/srv/data' (component prefix), so '/srv/data' is the longest and wins for both paths. No covering mount point occurs more than once in this mountinfo text ('/', '/srv' and '/srv/data' each appear exactly once), so the amendment's ambiguous_overmount refusal (unknown/n/a, fstype null, mount_point null, device_check not_checked) is NOT triggered. (3) Device - the amendment makes a device mismatch preempt the filesystem table; the chosen mount's major:minor is 0:25 and both reported paths carry st_dev '0:25', so the comparison is equal, device_check is 'match', and classification proceeds (the btrfs stat-major rule is not reached because the chosen fstype is xfs). (4) Classification - the amendment's xfs precedence is conflict first, then noquota, then any enforced key, then any accounting-only key, else absent; the super options split to keys rw, noquota, attr2, inode64, so 'noquota' is present and no quota/enforcement/noenforce key is present, which is the noquota row: quota_state 'disabled', enforcement 'n/a', basis 'xfs_noquota_option' (unchanged by the amendment; only the btrfs basis names changed). S077 (xfs.rst 171-173) backs the semantics of the key - 'noquota  Forcibly turns off all quota accounting and enforcement within the filesystem' - and S078 (xfs_super.c 239-254) backs that 'noquota' is a name the kernel itself emits in a mount's super-option string, while the same file's show_options guard 'if (!(mp->m_qflags & XFS_ALL_QUOTA_ACCT))' emits ',noquota' only when no scope has quota accounting on, so a kernel-emitted string never pairs 'noquota' with another quota key. (5) Decoys - the btrfs '/' line and the tmpfs '/srv' line lose the longest-prefix election for both reported paths, and the btrfs uuid in btrfs_sysfs is never consulted (under the amended btrfs rules that record would read as qgroups dir absent / enabled null, i.e. disabled/n/a/btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent or btrfs_qgroups_enabled_unavailable); the amendment's fixture source resolution (raw decoded source looked up in device_links, mapped basename otherwise basename(source), compared against the UUID devices lists) is satisfied structurally: '/dev/mapper/root' maps to 'dm-0' and the uuid lists ['dm-0'], and the xfs source '/dev/mapper/data' maps to the plain basename 'dm-1'. (6) Verdict - both reported paths are 'disabled', none is 'enabled' or 'unknown', and the fixture is well formed (nonempty unique normalized absolute paths, canonical decimal st_dev '0:25', canonical UUID key, plain basenames in devices and device_links values, exact bool/bool-or-null/mode-or-null qgroups field types, no extra record keys), so there is no setup error: exit 0 with finding_id 'QUOTA_DISABLED'.
